concepts.why: The patient presented with vision loss and severe macular changes with associated edema, and the OCT scans showed changes in macular edema over the course of treatment.
The patient had vision loss in the right eye and the fact that the reversible effect on cystoid macular edema was secondary to retinal vein occlusion after stopping niacin therapy.
The patient had a history of hypertension.
The patient had a history of hyperlipidemia.
The patient had a history of multiple strokes.
The patient's age and severe macular changes with associated edema are consistent with age-related macular degeneration.
It explains the reversible effect on cystoid macular edema secondary to retinal vein occlusion after stopping niacin therapy.

rationales.F02: History of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and multiple strokes increases the likelihood of C03, C04, and C05.
rationales.F06: Severe macular changes with associated edema are highly indicative of C01, C02, and C06.
rationales.F07: Persistent central macular thickness of 669.8 μm is a strong indicator of C01, C02, and C06.
rationales.F10: Reversible effect on cystoid macular edema secondary to retinal vein occlusion after stopping niacin therapy is a strong indicator of C01, C02, and C07.
